name: Origins Centre
funding: Wits campus museum, opened 2006; its Rock Art Research Institute is funded by the National Research Foundation, Wits' research fund and Anglo American's Chairman's Fund. No centre funder list.
watch: The draft's Arcadia and arts-department funding has no source.
records_note: The centre has no records of its own; parent Wits University posts annual reports 2006 to 2025 with audited accounts and lists its Council.

name: Ormston House
funding: The Arts Council of Ireland (An Chomhairle Ealaíon), Limerick City and County Council; non-profit cultural initiative.
watch: Cultural resource centre run by artists and curators, with environmental research on the River Shannon.

name: Owens Art Gallery
funding: 2023-24 public grants c. CAD 240k (Canada Council $180k, NB Tourism, Heritage & Culture $59k, Town of Sackville $1k) plus Mount Allison University; small private internship donors.
watch: Private names on the roster: Heather and Ian Bourne, the Jean and Peter Flemington Trust and J.E.A.
records_note: Posts annual reports for 2021-22 to 2025-26 and names internship donors; it has no accounts or board list, as part of Mount Allison University.

name: Oyoun
funding: Community support, independent non-profit foundation grants (Supporting Act Foundation), collective donations.
watch: Contested Berlin Senate funding withdrawal; July 2024 constitutional court procedural remand.

name: The Palestinian Museum
funding: Building (about US$24M, 2016) paid by 30-plus Palestinian families, Qattan Foundation, Bank of Palestine and the Arab Fund; Aliph funded a 2022 studio. No current donor list.
watch: Independent of Taawon since 2021. The claim that it takes no Palestinian Authority money has no source.
records_note: It posts annual reports for 2020 to 2022, a named founding-donor list and eleven board directors; no separate audited accounts found.

name: Pallas Projects/Studios
funding: The Arts Council of Ireland (An Chomhairle Ealaíon), Dublin City Council Arts Office; artist-run non-profit organisation.
watch: Founded in 1996 in the historic Coombe / Liberties area; Dublin’s longest-running independent artist-run space.

name: Palm Springs Art Museum
funding: Expenses $11.4M (FY2024); trustees, Bank of America, Sotheby's, Parker Palm Springs hotel, property firms, Pritzker for A+D.
watch: Sept 2024: three trustees quit over the director hire; a whistleblower alleged restricted endowment funds were misused (museum denies).
records_note: No annual reports; audited accounts and 990s for 2021 to 2024 are on its site, sponsors are undated logos, and the board is listed.

name: Papua New Guinea National Museum and Art Gallery
funding: A state statutory body funded by the PNG government. Australia paid for its 2015–2018 refurbishment, which reopened on 12 Oct 2018.
watch: Australia paid for the building in the 1970s and for its pre-APEC refit in 2018.
records_note: Its site is down; archived copies show no reports, accounts or funder list, and a Board of Trustees page that names no one.

name: Para Site
funding: Yenn and Alan Lo Foundation, Sunpride Foundation and Cheng-Lan Foundation lead the 2025 gala list. Galleries such as Gagosian, Zwirner and White Cube give; annual benefit auction and Patrons' Circle.
records_note: No annual report or accounts; it names benefactors of its 2025 gala and an undated patrons' circle, and lists a nine-person board plus advisors.

name: PAV - Parco Arte Vivente
funding: City of Turin Cultural Department, Regione Piemonte, Fondazione CRT; non-profit experimental art foundation.
watch: Experimental contemporary art center founded by Arte Povera artist Piero Gilardi, devoted to bio-art and ecology.

name: Paris Musées (Réseau des Musées de la Ville de Paris)
funding: City of Paris municipal budget covering 14 city museums (Carnavalet, MAM, Petit Palais, Catacombes, etc.).
